thread:
maria: FYI I'm seeing anchor links jump to the fenced codeblock instead of the H3. Likely slug collision with the triple-backtick fence. repro in PR: https://git/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2384 :eyes:
lee: ah yeah, I saw that pattern before with our docusaurus slugifier. fenced block language tags can sometimes create weird slugs when the heading is short.
tony: can you paste the minimal markdown snippet?
maria: sure — minimal repro below:

```markdown
### Run example
```python
print(\"hello\")
```
[Run example](#run-example)
```

maria: when the link is clicked it lands on the code fence instead of the heading text. Happens in both prod and local dev server.
lee: quick workaround is to add an explicit id on the heading: `### Run example {#run-example}` — docusaurus respects that.
olivia: fwiw adding explicit ids makes the source a bit noisy, but it's safest for stable anchors across toolchains.
lee: long-term fix is to normalize anchors during our doc build. we should avoid slug collisions from code fences.
tony: opened an infra ticket to check our markdown-it slug plugin config. Could be `slugify` mismatch between mkdocs and docusaurus.
maria: good — in the short term can we patch the PR to use explicit heading id? I can push a tiny commit.
lee: yes pls. also add a note in the PR description mentioning the anchor quirk so reviewers know why we forced the id.
maria: pushed patch with explicit id + test link. PR updated: https://git/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2384/files :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: CI: docs build started for PR #2384

deploy-bot: CI: docs build passed ✅
olivia: When we have a minute, let's add a docs checklist item: "if heading has ambiguous slug, add explicit {#id}". saves future debug.
lee: also adding a small unit test into our linkcheck pipeline to assert anchor targets aren't code fences (cheap).
tony: ticket filed: DOCS-812 — investigate slugifier parity and add linkcheck assertion.
maria: thanks all. I'll merge after the CI green and add the checklist item in a follow-up PR. :coffee:

lee: optional: if we want to be fancy we can strip language tag from fence slug generation in the plugin — but that's more invasive. open to RFC later.
maria: noted. night everyone.
